successors.name: Aztec Triple Alliance
successors.text: Tetzcoco and the Acolhua kingdoms of the eastern Basin

ledger.x: c. 1200: the Acolhua settle the eastern Basin of Mexico. 'arrived in the Valley of Mexico in or around the year 1200'; 'Their first capital was Coatlinchan'. The Texcoco page has 'Tetzcoco was founded in the 12th century... probably by the Chichimecs' and Xolotl as founder 'in 1115 AD'; 1202 is Cliopatria's year.…

c. 1337: the Acolhua take Tetzcoco and make it their capital. 'In or about 1337, the Acolhua, with Tepanec help, expelled Chichimecs from Tetzcoco'; 'Tetzcoco became the Acolhua capital city, taking over that role from Coatlinchan.'
c. 1337: the Acolhua capital moves from Coatlinchan to Tetzcoco (identity.capitals).
1418: Tezozomoc of Azcapotzalco dethrones the ruler of Texcoco.
1428: Nezahualcoyotl and the Mexica defeat Azcapotzalco.
1428: Texcoco joins Tenochtitlan and Tlacopan in the Triple Alliance.
1428: independent Texcoco ends as the second partner of the Aztec Triple Alliance (the tlatoani and the city continue to 1521).

wars.name: Tepanec domination and the Tepanec War
wars.outcome: Ixtlilxochitl I was dethroned by Tezozomoc in 1418; Maxtla turned on the Acolhua in 1426 and Nezahualcoyotl fled; in 1427-1428 the allies defeated Azcapotzalco and formed the Triple Alliance.

certainty.note: The pages give 'most of the eastern Basin of Mexico' only; no border is known.
